origin.description: One row per element of the shortest edit script, including the matches.
origin.usage: ses_dat(a, b, extra = TRUE, max.diffs = gdo("max.diffs"), warn = gdo("warn"))

arguments.name: extra
arguments.text: Add id.a and id.b. A match fills only id.a, because the value is taken from a.

arguments.name: max.diffs
arguments.text: Difference limit for the Myers search.

arguments.name: warn
arguments.text: Warn when the limit is hit.

origin.details: op is a factor with levels Match, Insert, and Delete. Inside a section, deletes come before inserts. val is the original element, so a missing value stays missing even though the comparison used the letters NA.
origin.value: A data frame with class ses_dat.
origin.example:
a <- letters[1:6]
b <- c("b", "CC", "DD", "d", "f")
ses_dat(a, b)

translation.description: The same rows. None is a missing value.

arguments.name: extra
arguments.text: Include id_a and id_b. A match fills only id_a.

arguments.name: max_diffs
arguments.text: Difference limit. None reads the option.

arguments.name: warn
arguments.text: Warn when the limit is hit. None reads the option.

translation.details: Each row is a dict. op is Match, Insert, or Delete. Indexes are 1-based. extra=False omits the index keys.
translation.example:
from diffobj import ses_dat
a = list("abcdef")
b = ["b", "CC", "DD", "d", "f"]
for row in ses_dat(a, b):
    ida = "NA" if row["id_a"] is None else row["id_a"]
    idb = "NA" if row["id_b"] is None else row["id_b"]
    print(row["op"], row["val"], ida, idb)
